# If player crashes into an enemy, both die

## Problem statement

When the player ship physically collides with an enemy entity, the enemy is not destroyed and the player only respawns — neither entity is properly handled. Per the GDD, the player loses one life when hit by **any** object (enemy body or enemy bullet), and the enemy should be destroyed. The current collision system is missing the player-vs-enemy-body check entirely.

## Users

- **Players** — expect that flying into an enemy destroys the enemy and costs the player one life (consistent with the GDD's "enemies are the bullets" hazard model).
- **AI agents / developers** — need the collision logic to match the documented behaviour so gameplay is consistent with the design.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want that if my ship crashes into an enemy, both the enemy and I are dealt with (enemy destroyed, I lose a life and respawn), so the game behaves as designed.
- As a **developer**, I want the collision system to handle player-vs-enemy-body in the same lifecycle as other collision cases (explosion VFX/SFX, respawn, invulnerability), so the code path is consistent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** — When the player ship overlaps an enemy entity (circle-vs-circle hit test using `Math.hypot <= rA + rB`), the enemy is destroyed via `destroySelf()` (and destruction audio is played).
- [ ] **AC2** — On the same collision event, the player is treated as "hit": destruction SFX + explosion VFX at the player position, respawn at spawn point, and a short invulnerability window (matching the existing enemy-bullet hit path).
- [ ] **AC3** — The player-enemy body collision check is added as a step in `GymFormationScene._handleCollisions()` (step 4, after enemy-bullets-vs-player), reusing the existing `_collide()` helper and `entityHitRadius` from `getEntityHitRadius()`.
- [ ] **AC4** — The player hit counter (`playerHitCount`) increments on collision, matching the existing enemy-bullet hit semantics. (Gym scenes use infinite lives; no formal lives counter.)
- [ ] **AC5** — All existing tests continue to pass; new unit tests cover player-vs-enemy-body collision (hit, miss, boundary).
- [ ] **AC6** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (this is a code-only change; the GDD already specifies the expected behaviour, so no docs edits required).
- [ ] **AC7** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The `_hitPlayer()` method correctly handles all side-effects of a player hit (VFX, SFX, respawn, invulnerability, hit counter). Verified against the enemy-bullet hit path.
- **Assumption:** The player ship has a defined hit radius (using `SHIP_SIZE / 2` as with bullets). If the player uses a different visual radius, the hit test should match.
- **Risk:** If the player is already respawning (invulnerability window active), a player-vs-enemy collision should probably be ignored (same as bullet hits). The existing `_hitPlayer()` already checks `playerInvulnerable > 0` implicitly via step 3.
- **Scope-creep guard:** This does not change enemy AI, bullet patterns, scoring, lives tracking beyond the hit counter, or Boss behaviour.

## Constraints

- **Reuse existing patterns.** The fix must follow the same code style and lifecycle as steps 1–3 in `_handleCollisions()`: circle-vs-circle hit test, `destroySelf()`, VFX/SFX, respawn + invulnerability.
- **Consistent with GDD §2.3.** The GDD explicitly states the player loses one life when hit by an enemy body; the fix must match this.
- **No scope creep.** This does not change enemy health, bullet damage, Boss behaviour, or scoring.

## Existing state

`GymFormationScene._handleCollisions()` (src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts) currently has three collision steps:

1. Player bullets vs enemies → enemy destroyed, bullet consumed ✓
2. Player bullets vs enemy bullets → both destroyed ✓
3. Enemy bullets vs player → explosion + respawn + invulnerability ✓

Step 4 (player body vs enemy body) is **missing entirely**.

## Desired change

Add a fourth collision step in `_handleCollisions()` that checks every alive entity against the player position using `_collide()` and the entity's hit radius. On collision: destroy the entity, play its destruction audio, trigger `_hitPlayer()` (explosion + respawn + invulnerability).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Add player-vs-enemy collision step to `_handleCollisions()`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — New test for player-vs-enemy-body collision
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — Already has `respawn()` method; may need life counter (verify)

## Related work

- **Clarify enemy health / one-hit destruction model in GDD (AH-0MT7V5UH90023XWR)** — Confirmed all regular enemies = 1 HP, destroyed by one hit.
- **Remove combo bonus from GDD and clarify lives model (AH-0MT7URFNN004Z01L)** — Clarified §2.3 collision model: "player loses one life when hit by any object (enemy or bullet)".

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions required — the GDD provides explicit specification for player-vs-enemy-body collision (§2.3).

# Change the teleport power-up (P7) activation key

## Problem Statement
The teleport power-up (P7) is currently activated with the Space key. It needs to be changed to the S key or the down arrow key per product requirement.

## Users
- Player controlling the ship in the GymPowerUpsCombat scene — needs to activate teleport with S or down arrow instead of Space.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **AC1 — New activation key:** The teleport power-up activates when the S key or down arrow is pressed (depending on clarification).
- **AC2 — Space key freed:** The Space key is no longer used for teleport activation (and continues to work for other purposes if applicable).
- **AC3 — GDD updated:** The Game Design Document (§3 Controls table, §4.4 P7 Teleport, §6.4) is updated to reflect the new key binding.
- **AC4 — Tests pass:** All existing tests pass; any tests that check for Space key triggering are updated.
- **AC5 — Full test suite passes.**

## Constraints
- Scope is the GymPowerUpsCombat.ts gym scene (main game scene scope TBD).
- Must maintain backward compatibility with test harness (triggerTeleport method).
- Must preserve the FIFO stack behavior and Phase Shift on arrival.

## Existing State
- Teleport activates on Space key (`spaceKey` in `GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` line 272).
- GDD documents Space as the activation key across multiple sections.

## Desired Change
- Change teleport activation from Space to S or down arrow key.
- Update GDD to reflect new key binding.

## Key Files (predicted)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — Change `spaceKey` to use S or down arrow
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update §3, §4.4, §6.4
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.test.ts` — Update any Space-key dependent tests

## Related Work
- AH-0MTE8EBZ1002U3PX — Unit tests: P7 Teleport (completed)
- AH-0MTE8EBAH007GUO0 — Effects module: teleport (completed)
- AH-0MTE8EBG3004QC66 — Combat gym scene with teleport (completed)

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Risk:** The S key is also used for movement (WASD). This could conflict with downward movement. *Mitigation: Clarify whether both S and down arrow should work, or just one.*
- **Assumption:** Only the gym scene needs updating; the main game scene does not yet have teleport activated.
- **Assumption:** Space key is not needed for shooting or other actions in the gym scene.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should teleport activate on EITHER the S key OR the down arrow key (both work)?" — Answer: **OPEN**
- Q: "Should it be the S key with down arrow as an alternative?" — Answer: **OPEN**
- Q: "Should the Space key still work for other actions (e.g., shooting)?" — Answer: **OPEN**
- Q: "Is the scope limited to the gym scene (GymPowerUpsCombat.ts), or should the main game scene also be updated?" — Answer: **OPEN**

# Make weapons cumulative and time out

## Headline

Replace the persistent weapon system with a cumulative, time-limited model: collecting a weapon power-up adds its firing effects to the ship's arsenal for 10 seconds, while the initial cannon remains permanent.

## Problem statement

The current weapon system uses a single-slot persistent model — collecting a weapon power-up **replaces** the currently equipped weapon with no timer. The operator has requested that weapons be **cumulative** (stacking effects) and **time out** after 10 seconds, with the exception of the initial cannon.

## Users

- **Player testing the game** — wants to collect multiple weapon power-ups and see their firing effects stack, then watch them expire one-by-one over 10 seconds, creating a dynamic and escalating combat experience.
- **Developer implementing the change** — needs a clear model for tracking multiple active weapons with individual timers and updating the Player entity, GymWeapons scene, and weapon utilities to support this behavior.

## Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to collect Spread while already firing the cannon so my ship fires *both* patterns, giving me more coverage without replacing my existing weapon.
- As a **player**, I want to see weapons I've collected time out after 10 seconds so that combat feels dynamic and power-ups create temporary bursts of capability rather than permanent upgrades.
- As a **player**, I want the initial cannon to **never time out** so I always have at least one reliable weapon.
- As a **player**, I want the Reset power-up to clear all timed weapons and leave only the cannon, giving me a way to "refresh" if I've lost all my timed weapons.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Cumulative weapons:** The Player entity tracks a **collection** of active weapons instead of a single equipped weapon. Collecting a weapon power-up adds it to the active set (no replacement). The cannon is always present in the active set.
- [ ] **AC2 — 10-second timeout per weapon:** Each weapon power-up (spread, dual, rapid) gets its own independent 10-second countdown from the moment of collection. When a timed weapon expires, it is removed from the active set and stops firing. The cannon has no timer and never expires.
- [ ] **AC3 — Auto-fire all active weapons:** On each fire cycle, the ship fires from **every active weapon** in the collection simultaneously. Each weapon fires at its own fire rate independently (e.g., rapid fires every 125ms, cannon every 400ms, spread every 600ms).
- [ ] **AC4 — Reset power-up clears timed weapons:** Collecting the Reset power-up removes all timed weapons (spread, dual, rapid) from the active set, leaving only the permanent cannon. The Reset power-up itself is not a weapon and is never added to the active set.
- [ ] **AC5 — GymWeapons scene updated:** The GymWeapons scene correctly handles the new cumulative model — collecting drops adds weapons to the active set, the Reset drop clears timed weapons, expired weapons are silently dropped, and auto-fire fires from all active weapons.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing:** Unit tests verify: weapon collection adds to active set, individual weapon timers count down and expire, expired weapons are removed, cannon never expires, Reset clears all timed weapons, auto-fire emits bullets from all active weapons at correct rates. Full suite green.
- [ ] **AC7 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the cumulative + timed weapon semantics (GDD §4.4 revision, code comments, README).
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). Neon-vector aesthetic.
- **Threat-free gym:** no enemies, no enemy bullets, no collision damage — player bullets are demonstration-only.
- **Backward compatibility:** the GymWeapons scene must continue to work with the new model.
- **Existing code to refactor:** Player.ts (single `_equippedWeapon` → weapon collection with timers), weapons.ts (add timeout tracking helpers if needed), GymWeapons.ts (collection logic update).

## Existing state

- `Player.ts` (`src/entities/Player.ts`): single `_equippedWeapon: WeaponId` slot, `equipWeapon()`, `resetWeapon()`, `tryFire()` fires one weapon.
- `weapons.ts` (`src/utils/weapons.ts`): weapon catalogue with definitions for cannon, spread, dual, rapid — all persistent, no timeout model.
- `GymWeapons.ts` (`src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`): `_collectDrop()` calls `player.equipWeapon()` or `player.resetWeapon()` — single-slot model.
- Weapon power-up drops: Spread, Dual, Rapid, Reset — round-robin, 7-second lifetime on screen.

## Desired change

1. **Player entity — weapon collection:** Replace `_equippedWeapon: WeaponId` with a weapon collection (e.g., a `Set<WeaponId>` for permanent weapons and a `Map<WeaponId, number>` for timed weapons tracking expiry timestamps). Update `equipWeapon()` to **add** to the collection, `resetWeapon()` to clear timed weapons.
2. **Player entity — auto-fire all weapons:** Update `tryFire()` to fire from **every active weapon** in the collection. Each weapon maintains its own cooldown. Emit bullets for all weapons whose cooldowns have elapsed this frame.
3. **Weapon timeout tracking:** Add per-weapon countdown logic. When a timed weapon's 10-second timer expires, remove it from the active set. Expose a method to tick and cull expired weapons.
4. **GymWeapons scene — updated collection:** Update `_collectDrop()` to call the new cumulative `equipWeapon()` (add, not replace). Reset clears timed weapons. No changes to the drop spawner itself.
5. **Constants:** Add a tunable `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000` constant (10 seconds) to `core/constants.ts`.
6. **Tests and documentation.**

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Player.ts` — major refactor: weapon collection with timers, multi-weapon auto-fire
- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — add timeout tracking helpers, possibly a `WeaponInstance` type with expiry
- `src/core/constants.ts` — add `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — update collection logic for cumulative model
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — new tests for cumulative weapon behavior
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.test.ts` — update tests for cumulative model

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — breaking GymWeapons tests:** The existing scene tests assert single-weapon behavior. They will need updates. Mitigated: tests are well-structured and the changes are contained to Player + GymWeapons.
- **Risk — auto-fire complexity with multiple weapons:** Each weapon has its own cooldown; the firing logic must track cooldowns per-weapon. Mitigated: straightforward extension of the existing cooldown pattern.
- **Risk — visual clutter from multi-weapon bullets:** With 3-4 weapons firing simultaneously, the screen may be visually busy. Mitigated: bullets have distinct colors per weapon (existing palette supports this).
- **Scope-creep risk:** HUD display for active weapons and remaining timers is **out of scope** — this is a gameplay mechanic change, not a UI change.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene" (completed): the item that implemented the current persistent single-slot weapon system. This item **refactors** that system.
- **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** — "Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD" (completed): generic power-up infrastructure.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Weapon stacking model — when collecting Spread while having cannon, does the ship fire BOTH patterns simultaneously (cannon + spread), and if then collecting Dual, does it fire ALL three (cannon + spread + dual)?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer response**.
- Q2: "Timeout granularity — does each weapon power-up get its own independent 10-second timer (e.g., Spread collected at t=0 expires at t=10, Dual collected at t=5 expires at t=15), or does picking up any weapon reset ALL active weapon timers to 10 seconds?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer response**.
- Q3: "Reset power-up behavior — with cumulative weapons, does Reset clear ALL timed weapons leaving only cannon, or does it work differently?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer response**.
- Q4: "Any visual/audio feedback on weapon expiration? Or do timed weapons simply stop firing when their timer expires?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer response**.

> All questions marked OPEN — waiting for producer review.

## Goal
Create the deterministic, pure-logic test suite that locks the explosion VFX contract before the implementation lands. Tests run without rendering and use a seeded RNG + fake timers.

## Context
Parent AH-0MTV6ADT4001FB2V needs a shared particle helper. This is the test-first feature — no implementation yet, just the spec suite that F2–F6 must satisfy. Keeps colour/pattern/geometry math pure and unit-testable per Constraints (Phaser 4.2.1 + Vitest).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **AC1:** Count scaling is locked: `scaledCount(size)` is linear with `size/referenceSize`, clamped to 8–80, verified at small (e.g. Swarm), standard (Scout/Diver/Tank/Phaser ~20–40) and large (Boss/player ~50–80) sizes.
- [ ] **AC2:** Colour jitter helper stays centred: 100% of emitted colours are within Δ around the base colour (HSL hue ±15–20°, slight sat/light variance); tested against all palette colours (SCOUT 0x00ff00, DIVER 0xffff00, TANK 0xff6600, PHASER 0xff00ff, SWARM 0x0066ff, BOSS 0xff0000, SHIP 0x00ffff).
- [ ] **AC3:** Geometry contracts asserted: radial burst spreads directions uniformly 0–2π with speed spread; ring emits at shared radius/speed forming a circle; implosion-then-burst has a short inward phase (~80–120 ms) then outward burst.
- [ ] **AC4:** Combinator splits verified: single pattern = 1/1, two patterns = 1/2+1/2, three patterns = 1/3+1/3+1/3 (remainder distributed deterministically).
- [ ] **AC5:** Lifecycle/teardown asserted: particles fade alpha 1→0 and shrink to 0 over 300–500 ms then auto-destroy; SHUTDOWN/teardown leaves zero leaked particles (fake timers + destroy spies).

## Key Files
- src/vfx/explosionParticles.test.ts

## Notes
Vertical slice Phase A tracer depends on this. Use seeded RNG so assertions are deterministic. No Phaser rendering in pure helpers.

# Player should spawn center screen

## Problem statement

In the enemy gym scenes, the player ship spawns at the top-right corner of the screen `(920, 30)` — behind the HUD area — instead of at center screen.

## Users

- **Players** — when entering an enemy gym scene, the player ship should be clearly visible and centered on screen, not tucked into a corner behind UI elements.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Center spawn:** The player ship spawns at the center of the game screen in all enemy gym scenes (GymEnemies, GymBoss, GymPowerUps, GymPowerUpsCombat, GymWeapons).
2. **AC2 — Consistent across all gym scenes:** The spawn position is uniform across every gym scene that includes a player ship.
3. **AC3 — Visible and unobstructed:** The spawn position places the player ship clear of any HUD elements and enemy formations.
4. **AC4 — Respawn consistency:** When the player is hit and respawns (in scenes that support hits), the respawn position matches the initial spawn position (center screen).
5. **AC5 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
6. **AC6 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- The change is a single constant update in `src/core/constants.ts` (`PLAYER_SPAWN`).
- The existing `GymBoss` scene already uses its own spawn coordinates (`BOSS_PLAYER_SPAWN_X`, `BOSS_PLAYER_SPAWN_Y` at center-bottom) and should remain unaffected unless specified otherwise.
- The `GymPlayer` scene already spawns at center screen and should be unaffected.

## Existing state

- `PLAYER_SPAWN` in `src/core/constants.ts` is set to `{ x: 920, y: 30 }` (top-right corner).
- The constant's comment explains the rationale: "clear of every formation and firing rightward off-screen so boot-time auto-fire never interferes with formation or wait-based tests."
- Used by: `GymEnemies.ts` (player toggle, config), `GymFormationScene` (base class), and related test files.
- `GymBoss` uses separate constants `BOSS_PLAYER_SPAWN_X` / `BOSS_PLAYER_SPAWN_Y` (center-bottom).

## Desired change

Update `PLAYER_SPAWN` to `{ x: GAME_WIDTH / 2, y: GAME_HEIGHT / 2 }` — i.e., `{ x: 480, y: 270 }` — so the player spawns at the center of the screen in enemy gym scenes.

Update the constant's comment to reflect the new intent.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/constants.ts` — Change `PLAYER_SPAWN` value and update its comment.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` — Uses `PLAYER_SPAWN`; tests may need updating.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Base class; player position derived from config.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — Tests reference `PLAYER_SPAWN` coordinates; may need updates.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts` — Tests assert player position against `PLAYER_SPAWN`; may need updates.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTHG5B83007W4W4** — Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (consolidated gym scene base class).
- **AH-0MTE8EBG3004QC66** — Combat gym scene: GymPowerUpsCombat.
- **AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9** — Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** Auto-fire on scene boot now fires from center screen instead of the edge. This could interfere with enemy formations earlier. **Mitigation:** The formation starts off-screen and drifts rightward; the player's bullets travel in the direction of travel (velocity heading), so this should be fine.
- **Assumption:** "Behind the hud bar" refers to visual obstruction at the top-right; center screen resolves this for all HUD configurations.
- **Assumption:** `GymBoss` should keep its existing center-bottom spawn position (its own constants are separate).
- **Risk:** Tests that assert specific player coordinates at scene start will need updating.

## Effort & Risk

- **Effort:** Small — single constant change + comment update + test adjustments.
- **Risk:** Low — the change is localized to spawn position; no new logic introduced.

data.description:
# Diver dive SFX (AH-0MTVYC6E8005YN6F)

**Headline:** Add two distinct procedural dive-phase sounds to the E2 Diver — a short "dive-start" cue played once at the FORMATION→DIVING transition, and a ~2-second continuous "dive whoosh" sustained for the dive duration — both wired entity-side in `Diver.ts` following the established `effects.ts` pattern.

## Problem statement

The E2 Diver entity (`src/entities/Diver.ts`) now has fire and destruction audio (AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG) but is silent on its signature behaviour: breaking formation and diving toward the player. The player gets no audible warning that a diver has begun its dive, and no sustained cue while the dive is in flight. Following GDD §7.3 enemy-audio feedback, add a distinct dive-start cue and a continuous dive sound, both distinguishable from the existing Diver fire (`playDiverFireSound`) and destruction (`playDiverDestructionSound`) sounds.

## Users

- **Players** — need an audible tell when a diver breaks formation (danger cue) and a sustained cue while the dive is in flight so the threat is trackable without watching every formation slot.
- **AI agents / developers** — need the sounds to follow the established procedural-audio pattern (`src/audio/effects.ts`) and degrade to safe no-ops in headless tests.

### Example user stories

- As a player, I want to hear a distinct cue the instant a diver breaks formation so I can react to the incoming dive.
- As a player, I want a sustained sound while the diver is diving so I can track the threat even when watching other enemies.
- As a developer, I want both sounds implemented via the existing `effects.ts` helpers so they degrade to safe no-ops in headless tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Dive-start cue** — A new `playDiverDiveStartSound()` exists in `src/audio/effects.ts`, played exactly **once per dive** at the FORMATION→DIVING transition (in `_startDive()`), distinct from the Diver fire and destruction sounds and from other enemies' cues.
- **Continuous dive sound** — A new sustained dive sound (start/stop pair or single ~2 s envelope matching `DIVER_DIVE_DURATION`) exists in `src/audio/effects.ts`, started at dive start and stopped when the dive ends (transition to RETURNING), so it plays for the whole dive and never leaks past it.
- **No leak on destruction/restart** — If the diver is destroyed mid-dive or the scene restarts mid-dive, the sustained dive sound stops (no orphaned oscillators). `destroySelf()` / `destroy()` and the SHUTDOWN teardown path must silence it.
- **Distinct character** — The two new sounds are distinct from each other AND from `playDiverFireSound()` / `playDiverDestructionSound()` (e.g. a rising whoosh/crack for dive-start, a sustained filtered-noise/sweep texture for the dive itself).
- **Safe degradation** — All new audio calls are safe no-ops without a working `AudioContext` (headless tests, browsers without Web Audio), preserving the `effects.ts` contract.
- **Tests** — New tests assert: dive-start cue fires exactly once per dive; the continuous sound starts at dive start and stops at dive end; no leak when destroyed mid-dive; degradation to no-op headless.
- **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README (if it lists per-enemy audio), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Procedural Web Audio only — no audio assets (existing `effects.ts` pattern).
- Follow enemy core-library best practices (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`).
- The continuous dive sound must have a bounded lifetime tied to the dive state machine (`DIVER_DIVE_DURATION = 2` s); it must not leak oscillators on destruction or scene restart (cf. `updateThrusterSound`/`stopThrusterSound` pattern for the player hum, and the SHUTDOWN teardown in AH-0MTPLHLZ3006MOC4).
- Multiple divers may dive concurrently — the dive-sound implementation must tolerate overlapping instances (per-dive nodes or a refcounted shared texture, implementer's choice, documented).
- Audio functions must degrade to safe no-ops in headless environments.
- Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — state machine `FORMATION → DIVING → RETURNING`; `_startDive()` transitions at the end of the hold timer (`DIVER_HOLD_FORMATION_SECONDS = 3`); `_handleDive()` advances `_divePhase` over `DIVER_DIVE_DURATION = 2` s then moves to RETURNING. Has `playDiverFireSound()` (once per spread burst) and `playDestructionAudio()` → `playDiverDestructionSound()`; **no dive-phase sounds exist**.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — has `playDiverFireSound()` (~280→120 Hz sawtooth crack, 80 ms) and `playDiverDestructionSound()` (280→40 Hz + sine undertone, 0.35 s); has the player thruster-hum start/stop/update sustained-sound pattern (`updateThrusterSound`/`stopThrusterSound`) as the precedent for a continuous sound; **no Diver dive sounds exist**.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — drives divers via `entity.applyFormationPosition(...)` in `tick()`; per-frame entity updates make an entity-side start/stop call site natural (no scene change expected).
- Reference: AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG ("Diver has no audio") — completed; added the fire + destruction sounds this item builds on.

## Desired change

- **New sounds**: add `playDiverDiveStartSound()` (short distinct cue, e.g. rising whoosh/crack) and a sustained dive-sound start/stop pair (e.g. filtered-noise/sweep texture, ~2 s, matching the dive duration) to `src/audio/effects.ts`, all safe no-ops without an `AudioContext`.
- **Diver entity**: call the dive-start cue exactly once in `_startDive()`; start the sustained sound on dive start and stop it when the dive ends (DIVING→RETURNING transition), in `destroySelf()`/`destroy()`, and anywhere the entity can be torn down mid-dive (null-scene guard precedent applies).

**Key Files:**

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — add `playDiverDiveStartSound()` + sustained dive-sound start/stop (procedural Web Audio, safe no-op guard; overlap-safe for concurrent divers).
- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — call dive-start cue once in `_startDive()`; start/stop the sustained sound with the DIVING state; silence it in `destroySelf()`/`destroy()`.
- `src/entities/Diver.test.ts` — dive-start once-per-dive test; sustained start/stop lifecycle test; no-leak-on-destroy test; headless no-op test.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — update the `GymDiver` audio row / audio section to mention the dive-phase sounds (if it lists per-enemy audio).
- `README.md` — update the `src/audio/effects.ts` bullet to mention the dive sounds (if per-enemy).

## Related work

- **Diver has no audio (AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG)** — completed; added Diver fire + destruction sounds. This item's sounds must be distinct from those.
- **Scout has no audio (AH-0MTCO1LDA008RA19)** — completed; sibling fire-sound + advance-cue item.
- **Swarm has no audio (AH-0MTCO1L74003CAQJ)** — completed; sibling burst-sound item.
- **Stale formation entities crash on GymEnemies scene restart (AH-0MTPLHLZ3006MOC4)** — completed; SHUTDOWN teardown precedent — relevant to the no-leak-on-restart requirement.
- **Player thruster hum (AH-0MTFOSOHN001Q620)** — completed; `updateThrusterSound`/`stopThrusterSound` sustained-sound precedent.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Continuous-sound lifecycle (medium)**: a sustained sound tied to a state machine can leak oscillators if the diver is destroyed or the scene restarts mid-dive. Mitigation: stop calls in `destroySelf()`/`destroy()` + SHUTDOWN teardown coverage; a no-leak test is an AC.
- **Concurrent divers (low)**: several divers may dive at once; overlapping sustained sounds must not corrupt shared module state. Mitigation: per-dive nodes or documented refcounting; implementer chooses and documents.
- **Distinctness is subjective**: "distinct" is judged by ear (different oscillator type / frequency range / envelope from fire + destruction). Mitigation: document the chosen character in code comments; reviewers listen in-browser.
- **Assumption**: entity-side wiring (no base-scene seam needed) — the dive lifecycle is fully inside `Diver.ts`, unlike destruction audio which the base scene owns. If the implementer finds a scene seam is needed, that is a small adjustment.
- **Scope creep**: no changes to fire/destruction sounds, no advance warning before the dive (producer: cue plays AT the transition), no other enemies' audio.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1**: Should the preparation sound play at the exact FORMATION→DIVING transition, or as an advance warning (≥ 500 ms lead)? — **Answer (producer): "at transition"** — the cue plays at the moment the Diver transitions (in `_startDive()`), not before. Source: interactive reply 2026-09-11.
- **Q2**: Should the dive sound be continuous through the ~2 s dive, or a short burst at dive start? — **Answer (producer): "continuous"** — a sustained sound for the whole dive duration, stopped when the dive ends. Source: interactive reply 2026-09-11.
- **Q3**: Should the two sounds be distinct from each other and from the existing Diver fire/destruction sounds? — **Answer (producer): "distinct"** — both new sounds are distinct from each other and from the existing palette. Source: interactive reply 2026-09-11.

**Research summary**: Inspected `src/entities/Diver.ts` (FORMATION→DIVING→RETURNING state machine; `_startDive()` transition point; `DIVER_DIVE_DURATION = 2` s; existing fire/destruction wiring, no dive-phase sounds), `src/audio/effects.ts` (existing `playDiverFireSound`/`playDiverDestructionSound`; player `updateThrusterSound`/`stopThrusterSound` sustained-sound precedent with no-op degradation), `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (entity driven per-frame via `applyFormationPosition` in `tick()` — entity-side wiring is natural, no scene seam expected), and the completed AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG item (fire + destruction sounds this item builds on).
